imageStudio.composer.unreachable: Server unreachable — is the backend running?
imageStudio.drop.body: They will be used as references for the next generation.
imageStudio.drop.title: Drop your images
imageStudio.help.aspect.body: Shape of the image: 1:1 square, 4:5 or 3:4 portrait, 16:9 wide landscape... "Reference" takes the format of the first attached image (and, at the "Original" definition, its resolution); reorder the images to change it. Without an attached image, it keeps the size of the last image made that way. An image smaller than the model's minimum is enlarged without distortion. "Custom" lets you type the width and height in pixels.
imageStudio.help.aspect.tip: choose the format before generating: cropping afterwards costs framing.
imageStudio.help.aspect.title: Format (width/height ratio)
imageStudio.help.attach.lead: Click, drag and drop or paste (⌘V).
imageStudio.help.attach.title: Attach images
imageStudio.help.megapixels.body: Total number of pixels of the image, in megapixels (MP). Higher = more detail and larger images, but computing and memory grow fast (2 MP ≈ 2 times slower than 1 MP). Beyond the size the model was trained on (~1 to 1.6 MP), compositions can duplicate.
imageStudio.help.megapixels.tip: look for the composition in "Draft" or "Standard", then redo it in "High" with the seed you like.
imageStudio.help.megapixels.title: Definition
imageStudio.help.references.tip: in the prompt, refer to the images by number: "the character of image 1 in the setting of image 2".
imageStudio.help.references.title: Reference images
imageStudio.help.sizeCustom.body: Exact width and height in pixels. The model works in fixed multiples (16, 32 or 64 px depending on the model): values are rounded, and bounded between a minimum and a maximum per side.
imageStudio.help.sizeCustom.tip: avoid very large sizes: prefer generating at ~1 MP, then upscaling.
imageStudio.help.sizeCustom.title: Custom size
imageStudio.home.subtitle: Describe an image, or drag in photos to transform them. Everything is computed on this machine.
imageStudio.notice.initOnly: {0} starts from a single image (img2img): only the 1st will be used. To combine several images, you need an editing model.
imageStudio.notice.maxReferences: {0} accepts at most {1} images: the following ones will be ignored.
imageStudio.notice.requiresReferences: {0} edits existing images: add at least one reference image.

imageStudio.quality.title: Definition
imageStudio.ref.help.face: Face to follow: the model draws the portrait after it ("Face likeness" setting). Put another image first to change it.
imageStudio.ref.help.faceStart: Start image, optional: the model redraws it (frame, composition) with the face of image 1. It also gives the "Reference" format.
imageStudio.ref.help.image: Image {0}: refer to it this way in the prompt.
imageStudio.ref.help.initIgnored: Ignored: this model starts from a single image, the 1st one.
imageStudio.ref.help.multiIgnored: Ignored: this model accepts at most {0} images.
imageStudio.ref.help.none: {0} does not use reference images: this one will have no effect.
imageStudio.ref.help.start: Start image: the model transforms it according to your prompt (img2img).
imageStudio.ref.moveFirst: Move first (its format and resolution become the reference)
imageStudio.send.tip.incompatible: Model not compatible with this machine
imageStudio.size.remembered: Size of the last image made from a reference. Add an image to follow its format.
imageStudio.size.rounding: Rounded to a multiple of {0} px · from {1} to {2} px per side.
